topic: Combining Atomic/Volatile for Concurrent Memory-Mapped I/O
explanation: While `std::atomic` and `volatile` typically serve different masters, they can be combined for highly specialized tasks, specifically involving memory-mapped I/O (MMIO). When an MMIO location is concurrently accessed by multiple threads, both guarantees are necessary: `volatile` ensures the compiler interacts directly with the memory location (preventing optimization), and `std::atomic` ensures the concurrent accesses are properly synchronized and ordered across different threads.
practical_example: Writing a device driver where multiple application threads might simultaneously update a status register residing in memory-mapped I/O space. Failure to use both attributes results in either data races (if `volatile` only) or incorrect hardware interaction (if `atomic` only).
keywords: atomic volatile MMIO, concurrent memory-mapped I/O, atomic volatile combination, hardware registers synchronization
chapter: Item 40: Use std::atomic for data accessed from multiple threads without using mutexes.
book: Effective Modern C++ by Scott Meyers
